human_tolerance.notes: A familiar bird of gardens, parks, woodland edges and suburban areas, where dense cover is interspersed with open ground; a regular visitor to bird feeders and a common nester in garden shrubs and vine tangles.

phases.name: breeding
phases.note: Two to four broods are raised each year, from spring into late summer; exact start/end dates are a judgement placed around the described breeding season.

phases.name: territorial
phases.note: Pairs hold a territory year-round; the male sings from a high perch to defend it in all months.

vocalizations.description: Clear, whistled, repeated phrases such as 'cheer-cheer-cheer' and 'purdy-purdy-purdy'; both sexes sing, and the male sings from a high perch to defend his territory.
A short, distinctive metallic chip, given when a predator approaches the nest to warn the female and nestlings.

common_names.note: en label from Wikidata; fr/de labels are Wikidata sitelink-derived labels for Q726389.

range.note: Native country list read off the Distribution and habitat section ('numerous across the eastern United States ... in Canada in the southern portions of Ontario, Quebec, New Brunswick and Nova Scotia ... south through Mexico to the Isthmus of Tehuantepec, northern Guatemala, and northern Belize'). Bermuda (BM) listed as introduced from the same section; Hawaii is part of the US and not listed separately.

traits.locomotion_modes.note: 'It is a ground feeder and finds food while hopping on the ground through trees or shrubbery'; a strong flier.

traits.nest_type.note: An open cup of twigs, grass and plant fibres built in thick shrubs, trees and vine tangles.

traits.perching.note: A territorial songbird that sings from the top of a tree or another high location.

traits.mass_kg.note: 'The adult weighs from 33.6-65 g (1.19-2.29 oz), with an average 44.8 g (1.58 oz).'

traits.length_m.note: Midpoint of 'a body length of 21-23.5 cm'.

traits.lifespan_y.note: 'Annual survival rates for adult northern cardinals have been estimated at 60-65%'; using the midpoint p=0.625 and the constant-hazard approximation 1/(1-p) gives about 2.7 years, rounded to 3. The banded record (15 years 9 months) is a maximum, not a typical lifespan.

traits.diet.note: Wikipedia: the adult diet is 'up to 90% of weed seeds, grains, and fruits', with snails and insects (beetles, cicadas, grasshoppers) as the remainder, and nestlings fed almost entirely on insects. EltonTraits is consistent (primarily granivore/frugivore with some invertebrate prey). Shares are a rounded judgement between the two.

traits.social.note: Mated pairs generally stay together year-round and hold a territory; group_size [1,2] is judgement.

traits.activity_pattern.note: Feeding, song and territorial behaviour are all described by day; no nocturnal activity is described.

traits.defense.note: Authored: the bird flushes and flees when a predator approaches, and gives a chip alarm call.

traits.wariness.note: Judgement: fairly tolerant of people, feeding close to houses and at feeders, but warier than a house sparrow.

habitat.use.note: Judgement split: a ground feeder that forages by hopping, but nests, sings and roosts in shrubs and trees, so a little more time is spent off the ground than on it.

habitat.shelter_tag.note: Nests and shelters in 'thick and dense shrubs, trees, and vine tangles'; shrub_thicket is the closest tag.

habitat.resources.note: Food weights follow traits.diet; nest_cup, perch, shrub_thicket and water weights are qualitative from the nest and habitat descriptions.

habitat.human_tolerance.note: urban_affinity, uses_gardens and the notes follow the described abundance in 'parks, and suburban areas' and at feeding stations; light_max and road_mortality are judgement.

seasonal.strategy.note: Resident year-round; no migration or dormancy is described.

seasonal.phases.note: Breeding season and two-to-four broods a year are from Wikipedia; the exact phase start/end dates and the year-round territorial phase are judgement.

seasonal.life_stages.note: Incubation 12-13 days and fledging 10-11 days after hatching; duration_days (40) and scale are a judgement approximation of time to independence, not a sourced figure.

look.note: Modelled on the male: vibrant red plumage, black face mask and a prominent crest, with a lighter red breast and darker red wings and tail. Proportions and extra-part placement are judgement; the female (reddish olive with a grey mask) is not modelled.

behavior.note: Authored parameters for the shared perching-songbird program: seed-based ground foraging, a March-September nest window reflecting two to four broods, a moderate flee distance, and call ids matching the song/chip vocalizations above.
